name: Bramble
description: Gin, lemon and sugar over crushed ice, with blackberry liqueur drizzled through the top.
history: Dick Bradsell created it at Fred’s Club in London in the 1980s, thinking of blackberry-picking on the Isle of Wight. It is one of the few modern British classics.
whyItWorks: A plain gin sour made fruity at the last moment. The liqueur bleeds down through the ice, so the drink gets sweeter and darker as you go.
steps: Shake gin, lemon and simple syrup with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass packed with crushed ice.
Drizzle the crème de mûre over the top so it bleeds down.
Garnish with a lemon slice and a blackberry.
techniqueNotes: Crème de cassis is the common stand-in if you can’t find crème de mûre.
creator: Dick Bradsell
